Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic agent commonly used to treat hypertension, chronic edema from congestive heart failure or cirrhosis, and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. results.text: Ritodrine-associated Noncardiogenic Pulmonary Edema Diagnosed by Point-of-care Ultrasound: A Case Report of Twin Gestation. Ritodrine hydrochloride, a beta-adrenergic tocolytic agent, can rarely cause acute noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, particularly in patients with multiple gestations or comorbidities. We report a case of a 28-year-old woman with twin pregnancy, type 1 diabetes, and hyperthyroidism that developed acute respiratory distress following ritodrine infusion.
